messages:
maya: heads-up — ran into a parity problem between REST streaming and the node-sdk streaming helper when using function-calling. REST stream sends newline-delimited JSON chunks ("\n" separated), but the sdk's stream parser expects SSE-style `data:` frames. result: functions payloads get split mid-json and our sampleapp throws JSON.parse errors. repro snippets below.

maya: curl (server stream, works):
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"chat-fn","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"run me"}]}'
# stream chunks look like:
# {"type":"message","delta":{"role":"assistant"}}
# {"type":"message","delta":{"content":"start {\"func\":\"x\",\"args\":{\"a\":1}} end"}}
# {"type":"done"}
```

maya: node-sdk (broken):
```js
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'chat-fn', messages: [...] })
stream.on('data', chunk => {
  // our parser emits split pieces like 'start {"func":"x","args":{' and '"a":1}} end' causing JSON.parse to fail
})
```

maya: hypothesis: when the server switches between chunk boundaries the sdk's SSE-only parser doesn't reassemble chunks that are not prefixed with `data:` lines. the REST curl client just prints raw bytes and human readers rejoin them.

owen: reproduces locally. looks like the SDK's stream helper was implemented with an eventsource mindset (data: lines) because older streaming endpoints used SSE. newer runtime uses raw chunked transfer with ":\n" separators. we should be tolerant of both.

jun: also observed that our automatic retry middleware treats stream errors (partial parse) as transient and retries the whole request, which ends up calling the target function twice for some workflows. customer saw duplicate side-effect from function-calls (created two db rows). so two issues: parser fragility + aggressive retrying on non-idempotent streamed calls.

eli: proposal: 1) update node-sdk stream parser to accept both SSE (`data: ...\n\n`) and raw newline-delimited JSON (split on /\r?\n/ and reassemble incomplete json objects before emitting). 2) make the retry layer not retry streaming requests by default (or only retry for idempotent endpoints) and expose an opt-in `idempotent: true` flag. 3) add integration e2e in sampleapp that uses function-calling over streams to catch dupes.

owen: quick patch I validated: buffer incoming bytes, split on newline, attempt JSON.parse on the accumulated buffer, if parse fails due to EOF, wait for more bytes instead of emitting error. also gate retries: only retry for status >=500, not for parse errors from streaming.

jun: add tests: one that emits split-chunked json across two writes and assert sdk emits single parsed message; another that simulates a parse error and asserts no retry and error surfaced to caller. Also add a migration note in streaming guide.

maya: thanks. can we also scan other sdks (python/go) for the same parser assumption? might be a template-level bug in codegen for streaming helpers.

eli: will open coordinated issues and assign owners. tagging @devex-bot.

devex-bot: Created issue #4012: "node-sdk streaming: support raw chunked newline-delimited JSON in addition to SSE; prevent retries on streaming parse errors to avoid duplicate function calls" assigned to owen, priority: high. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4012 :white_check_mark:

maya: follow-up: add a tiny CI e2e in onboarding sample that hits streaming function-call once and asserts single side-effect. low-effort but catches this quickly.

owen: will open PR with parser fix + tests + changelog entry. ping here when ready. :thumbsup:
